prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but the “best” installer depends on your exact location, budget, and priorities (speed, brand, efficiency, warranty). If you tell me your ZIP code and whether this is a home or a business, I’ll pull a short list of well-rated companies in your area and compare quotes/options.

Meanwhile, here’s a quick guide to find the best HVAC company in Atlanta and what to ask:

What to ask and check
- Ask for proof they’re licensed and insured. (Also confirm they carry general liability and worker’s comp.)
- Ensure techs are EPA 608 certified (required to handle refrigerants) and preferably NATE‑certified.
- Request a written, itemized estimate (equipment, labor, permits, disposal).
- Make sure they perform a Manual J load calculation to size the system properly — don’t accept a one-size-fits-all recommendation.
- Ask about equipment brands and model SEER ratings, and whether they’re an authorized dealer for those brands.
- Get details on warranties (parts and labor) and whether they offer a service/maintenance plan.
- Ask if they pull permits and handle local inspections.
- Confirm timeline for ordering, installation, and cleanup/disposal of the old unit.
- Ask about financing options, utility rebates, and tax credits they can help you claim.

Red flags
- Very low ball estimates without a written scope.
- Pressure to sign right away or sales-only visits without a load calculation.
- No references or very few online reviews.

How to compare quotes
- Compare total installed cost, but weigh warranty, brand reliability, and the quality of the installation.
- Prefer companies that include startup/commissioning and explain thermostat compatibility, airflow adjustments, and ductwork concerns.
- Aim for at least three written quotes.

Typical cost ranges (Atlanta, approximate)
- Small replacement (2–3 ton, basic unit): roughly $3,500–$6,000 installed.
- Mid-range/high-efficiency systems or larger homes: $6,000–$10,000+.
(Actual price depends on system size, brand, SEER rating, ductwork condition, and complexity.)

If you want, give me your ZIP code and any preferences (brand, budget, timeline), and I’ll list 3–5 well-rated local installers, summarize their strengths, and what to expect from each.
